extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials, rulewriters, and stakeholders (advocacy groups, industry, experts) who participate in or design public engagement for rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for how federal agencies should plan, structure, and execute public engagement across the rulemaking lifecycle, and advice for outside commenters on when and how to engage. Emphasizes early, targeted, and structured outreach beyond the baseline notice-and-comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic planning and early engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal engagement policies; plan participation as early as feasible, including problem identification and priority-setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should adopt strategic planning for engagement so that participation occurs in agenda-setting and early development stages rather than only at the formal proposal stage. Early engagement should include problem identification and setting priorities, not merely reacting to a published proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overreliance on notice-and-comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice-and-comment is often 'dominated by certain sophisticated stakeholders' and agencies rely too heavily on it as the default mode of public participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat the formal comment period as the only meaningful input channel. Recognize that relying solely on the Federal Register process risks skewed participation and misses other stakeholder voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted outreach to underrepresented stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Proactively reach stakeholders who traditionally are absent because 'not everyone reads the Federal Register.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must undertake outreach beyond passive publication—identify groups unlikely to monitor the Federal Register and use tailored channels and messaging to engage them, rather than assuming broad awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use advance information requests and ANPRMs/RFIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ information requests / advance notices before formal proposals (e.g., ANPRMs, RFIs) to gather upstream input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should issue advance notices and targeted information requests to solicit input before committing to a regulatory frame. Commenters should watch for ANPRMs and RFIs and respond upstream because high-leverage windows often occur before the formal proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted outreach to experts and non-traditional participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliberately solicit input from technical experts and 'non-traditional participants' who can provide specialized or unique perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design outreach that identifies and recruits both domain experts and stakeholders outside usual interest groups. Use targeted invitations, expert panels, or bespoke consultation to surface technical information and lived-experience insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convening diverse groups for dialogue on regulatory alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold convenings that bring diverse participants together to discuss and deliberate about regulatory alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use workshops, focus groups, or deliberative forums to enable interactive discussion of policy options. Structure these convenings to promote inclusion, manage power imbalances, and focus on exploring alternatives rather than merely presenting a predetermined proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel trained in public engagement best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff involved in engagement should be trained in public engagement best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in training for personnel so they can design and facilitate effective outreach, structure meetings, and interpret stakeholder input appropriately. Trained staff improve the quality and accessibility of engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carefully structured meetings with accessible background materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Meetings should be carefully structured and accompanied by accessible background materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear agendas, facilitation plans, and plain-language background documents so participants understand context and can contribute meaningfully. Accessible materials reduce information barriers and increase the quality of input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic assessment of stakeholders' information needs and gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess what information stakeholders lack at each stage and tailor engagement to fill those gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before outreach, identify the specific informational deficits among targeted participants and design activities or materials to address them. This makes engagement more efficient and increases the likelihood of receiving useful, informed input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-effective selection of engagement tools based on information value
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose engagement tools that are cost-effective given their potential to generate valuable information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh the cost of each engagement method against expected informational return. Prioritize tools that maximize useful, actionable input relative to their resource requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalize and structure ad hoc early-engagement efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: Many early-stage interactions have been 'unstructured and ad hoc'—agencies should formalize these practices into predictable policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert informal listening sessions and ad hoc upstream contacts into documented policies and procedures so that early engagement is systematic, predictable, and consistently inclusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implication for outside commenters: engage upstream, not only during formal comment periods
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit during the formal comment phase only, you've missed high-leverage windows; watch for ANPRMs, RFIs, and informal listening sessions and engage upstream when the agency hasn't committed to a frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders seeking influence should monitor agency agenda-setting and early outreach opportunities and participate in advance notices, information requests, and convenings rather than relying solely on post-proposal comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratizing the regulatory process through comprehensive information gathering
rubrics_metrics.description: The ultimate goal is 'democratizing the regulatory process' by expanding participation and gathering comprehensive information from diverse publics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate engagement success by how well it expands access, captures diverse experiences and knowledge, and reduces control of the process by a narrow set of sophisticated stakeholders. Prioritize practices that enhance legitimacy and inclusiveness.
